Select Vegetation Clusters Using Modified TWINSPAN and OptimClass

Source: R/twinspan_optimclass_ecan.R
twinspan_optimclass_ecan.Rd

Generates vegetation partitions using Modified TWINSPAN and selects the number of clusters according to OptimClass 1 or OptimClass 2, based on statistically significant species-to-cluster fidelity.

Usage

twinspan_optimclass_ecan(
  veg,
  cut_levels = c(0, 2, 5, 10, 20),
  min_size = 5,
  k_values = 2:20,
  p_threshold = 0.05,
  min_faithful = 3,
  version = c("fast", "original"),
  select_by = c("optimclass1", "optimclass2"),
  show_plots = TRUE
)

Arguments

veg

A numeric vegetation matrix or data frame, with relevés (sampling plots) in rows and species in columns. Row names and column names must be present, non-empty, and unique. Values must be finite, non-negative, and free of missing values; zero indicates species absence.

cut_levels

Numeric vector of cover cut levels for TWINSPAN pseudospecies. Default is c(0, 2, 5, 10, 20).

min_size

Positive integer specifying the minimum cluster size passed to ecan::twinspan(). Default is 5 relevés.

k_values

Integer vector of cluster numbers to evaluate. Default is 2:20. Values not yielding valid partitions are excluded.

p_threshold

Fisher's exact test significance threshold used to identify faithful species. Must be strictly between 0 and 1. Default is 0.05.

min_faithful

Positive integer specifying the minimum number of faithful species required for a cluster to contribute to OptimClass 2. Default is 3.

version

Fidelity computation method. "fast" uses the upper tail of the hypergeometric distribution with stats::phyper(); "original" uses stats::fisher.test(). Both implement an equivalent one-sided Fisher exact test (alternative = "greater"). Default is "fast". Code from Monteiro-Henrique. (2025)

select_by

Selection criterion for the final partition: "optimclass1" (default) or "optimclass2".

show_plots

Logical; whether to print both OptimClass plots. Default is TRUE.

Value

A named list containing:

  • results: Data frame summarizing each valid k: OptimClass 1 (optimclass1), OptimClass 2 (optimclass2), proportion of qualifying clusters (prop_good_clusters), minimum group size (min_group_size), and optimum indicators (best_optim1, best_optim2).

  • best_k: List of all optimal k values under optimclass1 and optimclass2, including ties.

  • selected_k: Number of clusters selected for the final partition.

  • selected_by: Criterion used for final selection.

  • classification: Data frame with stand and group columns for the selected partition.

  • classification_all: Data frame with k, stand, and group for every valid partition.

  • partitions: List of named cluster membership vectors for each k.

  • faithful_species: Table of significant species-cluster associations in the selected partition (k, group, species, p_value).

  • faithful_species_all: Table of significant species-cluster associations across all valid partitions.

  • faithful_by_group: Named list of faithful species for each selected cluster.

  • fidelity: Per-partition matrices p_values and faithful (species by cluster), plus faithful_per_group counts.

  • plots: List with optimclass1 and optimclass2 ggplot objects.

  • failed_k: Candidate values of k without a valid partition.

  • settings: List of parameters used for the analysis.

Details

The function performs Modified TWINSPAN with ecan::twinspan() for every candidate number of clusters in k_values. Species cover values are used by TWINSPAN, while species fidelity is evaluated on a presence/absence matrix derived from veg.

For each species and each cluster, fidelity is assessed using a one-sided Fisher exact test against all other clusters. Species with a p-value less than or equal to p_threshold are counted as faithful. This function uses p-values rather than the standardized Phi coefficient. It does not apply multiple-testing correction.

OptimClass 1 is the number of unique species that are significantly faithful to at least one cluster. OptimClass 2 is the number of clusters containing at least min_faithful significantly faithful species. Each criterion is maximized separately.

All tied optimal values of k are retained in best_k. For the final classification, the smallest optimal k is chosen under select_by. The number of clusters is optimal only with respect to the candidate partitions and the chosen fidelity threshold; ecological and syntaxonomic validation remains necessary.

The function relies on ecan for Modified TWINSPAN and ggplot2 for plotting. Their namespaces must be available.

References

Roleček, J., Tichý, L., Zelený, D., & Chytrý, M. (2009). Modified TWINSPAN classification in which the hierarchy respects cluster heterogeneity. Journal of Vegetation Science, 20, 596–602. doi:10.1111/j.1654-1103.2009.01062.x

Tichý, L., Chytrý, M., Hájek, M., Talbot, S. S., & Botta-Dukát, Z. (2010). OptimClass: Using species-to-cluster fidelity to determine the optimal partition in classification of ecological communities. Journal of Vegetation Science, 21, 287–299. doi:10.1111/j.1654-1103.2009.01143.x

Monteiro-Henriques, T. (2025). TDV-optimization: A novel numerical method for phytosociological tabulation. Vegetation Classification and Survey, 6, 99–127. doi:10.3897/VCS.140466

See also

ecan::twinspan(), stats::fisher.test(), stats::phyper()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Vegetation matrix: relevés in rows, species in columns
data("dune", package = "vegan")

res <- twinspan_optimclass_ecan(
  dune,
  k_values = 2:10,
  min_size = 2,
  select_by = "optimclass1",
  show_plots = FALSE
)

res$best_k
res$selected_k
head(res$classification)
head(res$faithful_species)
res$plots$optimclass1
res$plots$optimclass2

# Partition chosen using OptimClass 2
k2 <- min(res$best_k$optimclass2)
subset(res$classification_all, k == k2)
} # }
